title: Costing model and quota bucketing for partially-cached interleaved KV/prefix hits
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:

When coalesced request batches include a mix of fully cached prefixes, partial KV cache hits, and non-cached requests, our existing metering pipeline either (a) double-charges token-equivalents for requests that triggered upstream fetches in shared batches, or (b) undercounts quota usage for partially cached responses because token attribution is per-request rather than per-execution-unit. This leads to incorrect quota enforcement, surprising billing spikes for customers that rely on prefix caching, and race conditions with the rate limiter when token budgets are depleted mid-batch.

Goal:
Define and implement a clear, auditable costing model and quota bucketing strategy that: (1) attributes chargeable units deterministically for mixed cache-hit batches; (2) integrates with the rate limiter to avoid under/over-throttling; (3) preserves expected zero-cost behaviour for pure cache hits; (4) is efficient to compute in the real-time metering path and backwards-compatible with historical reports where possible.

This ticket captures design, implementation tasks, test plans, and rollout/migration considerations. This is distinct from prior work which normalized prefetch/coalesced batch metering; the focus here is on interleaved partial KV/prefix hits within the same batch and quota-bucket interactions across tenants.
acceptance_criteria: New costing model defined and documented with examples for common edge cases (full hit, partial hit, cross-tenant coalesced fetch).

Metering pipeline emits per-execution charge records that contain: batch_id, execution_unit_tokens, cache_hit_type (full|partial|miss), originating_request_ids, and attribution_policy (request|execution).
Rate limiter consults execution-level cost estimate prior to admitting a batch; if admitting will exceed a tenant's quota, admission is partial-fail with clear retryable status returned to callers.
Billing reports (daily) match sampled ground-truth from instrumented traces within 0.5% for mixed-cache workloads in performance tests.
No customer-facing quota regressions after canary rollout to 5% of clusters for 48 hours.
Automated integration tests that replay synthetic coalesced batches with deterministic cache-hit patterns and assert quota accounting and throttle outcomes.
implementation_plan: Design: formalize 'execution unit' as the atomic chargeable entity (one kernel-run / one fetched token-segment) and three cache_hit_type enums.
Schema: add lightweight metering tags to runtime request context (cache_hit_type, execution_estimated_tokens, source_model_variant, batch_id, originating_request_ids).
Metering pipeline changes: compute execution-level records in the runtime, surface to ingestion with minimal post-processing, ensure idempotency keys for retries.

Rate limiter change: estimate admission cost by summing execution_estimated_tokens for non-full-hit units in batch; consult per-tenant bucket before enqueueing; expose partial-admit path that returns a 429 variant with 'retry-after-execution' metadata.

Billing aggregation: aggregate execution records into per-request charges by applying attribution_policy (default: execution attribution for any non-full-hit token; requests that were pure full-hit remain zero-cost).
Backward compatibility: maintain existing per-token billing for hosted customers by keeping a compatibility shim at the aggregator layer for 90 days after rollout.
Instrumentation: add OLAP counters and trace spans to verify behavior (execution_counts_by_cache_hit, throttled_batches_by_tenant, retrocharge_adjustments).
PRs: split into runtime change, metering ingestion change, rate-limiter change, billing aggregator adjustment, console/reporting updates.
migration_plan: Canary rollout: enable execution-level metering on a small fleet (5% of traffic) with 'billing-preview' flag for affected tenants to surface predicted charges in the Console but not invoice them.
Shadow aggregation: run new aggregator in parallel to existing billing for 14 days and compare diffs; create automated anomaly alerts if diffs exceed thresholds per-customer.
Retrocharge policy: if a customer is overcharged during migration, flag cases for manual review and automated credits; log all retrocharge candidates with reasons.
Opt-out: provide a temporary escape hatch 'legacy_charge_model' tenant flag for enterprise customers during the 90-day migration window.
Full cutover: after validation, flip default to new model and deprecate legacy shim after 90 days.
test_plan: Unit tests for execution-level token accounting logic with randomized sequences of cache-hit patterns.
Integration tests that simulate mixed-tenant coalesced batches across our GPU pool and assert consistent metering records even under retries/timeouts.
Load test: synthetic workload with 1M coalesced batches/hour, 40% partial hits, ensure metering pipeline latency additions < 5ms P95 and no increased tail latency for inference path.
Property tests verifying idempotency of metering records under duplicate submission scenarios.
E2E canary checks that compare Console preview billing vs legacy aggregator; require parity thresholds before promoting rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: increased runtime latency when computing execution_estimated_tokens. Mitigation: compute conservative estimates (upper bounds) in hot path and refine asynchronously for invoiced records.
Risk: customers see unexpected invoice deltas. Mitigation: long preview window, detailed Console breakdown, customer support playbook and credits automation.
Risk: race with rate limiter leading to partial admissions and client errors. Mitigation: define clear retryable status, backoff guidance in SDKs, and telemetry to surface patterns.
comments: 2026-02-11 Marco Ruiz: Initial review complete. We need clarity on whether 'partial hit' should be charged proportional to token fetch or to the fetches' cost bucket. I prefer execution attribution so that shared fetches are charged once per execution and split across originating requests by 'request weight' later in billing reports.

2026-02-18 Priya Shah: Product agrees that zero-cost semantics must be preserved for pure prefix-only cache responses. Suggest adding a Console flag 'preview_new_billing' exposed to enterprise tenants.

2026-02-22 Ben Carlson: POC runtime change merged to feature branch (runtime/metering/exec-attr). Microbenchmarks show +1.8ms median and +3.9ms p95 on hot path — acceptable but add optimization pass to inline the estimator.
2026-02-27 Ops: Can we schedule a 48h canary during low-us traffic window? Proposed: 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-12 on region us-west1. Added to deployment calendar.
2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include 'billing reports match sampled ground-truth within 0.5%'. Moved status to Planned; next: split PRs and assign owners for each subsystem.
